selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What invitation does the earth give the traveler at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It calls him away from wandering through the sky and tells him to examine the earth’s works and learn from them.

questions.question: What do the earth’s two motions accomplish in the passage?
questions.answer: They organize the passing of time through day, year, and season.

questions.question: Why is the earth described as a great ship?
questions.answer: Because it carries huge amounts of supplies and necessities for living creatures while traveling in space in a balanced way.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from even one page of the earth?
questions.answer: He learns that it contains many signs pointing to the One who sustains it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the origin of many life-forms in spring?
questions.answer: Their many shapes come out from simple matter with great precision.

questions.question: How is nourishment described in relation to mercy?
questions.answer: Food is presented as being provided gently, generously, and with compassion.

questions.question: What contrast is used to show divine power in providing food?
questions.answer: Delicious foods are produced from plain earth and from similar-looking roots, seeds, and drops of fluid.

questions.question: How does the example of milk for infants deepen the message of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a close, human example of loving care that people can easily recognize.

questions.question: What larger belief does the revival of the earth in spring support?
questions.answer: It supports belief that the One who revives dead land can also raise the dead.

questions.question: What is meant by calling spring a visible proof of resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring lets people watch a kind of small-scale return to life that points to the final rising of the dead.

questions.question: Why does the earth tell the traveler to look at its functions and pages?
questions.answer: It wants to show him the signs that answer what he has been seeking.

questions.question: How does the description of the earth’s motion combine movement and order?
questions.answer: Although it is constantly turning, it does so in a way that produces stable patterns for life.

questions.question: Why does the traveler not try to read every page of the earth?
questions.answer: Because its signs are too many, so he chooses one page to study closely.

questions.question: What is significant about the phrase that forms emerge from simple material?
questions.answer: It points to the difference between plain substance and the highly ordered living shapes that come from it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from seeds being spread in effective ways?
questions.answer: Their movement serves a purpose and is managed with knowledge and planning.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress the variety of foods?
questions.answer: To show the richness of provision given to creatures with different needs.

questions.question: Why is a mother’s milk presented as a strong proof of compassion?
questions.answer: Because it is specially prepared for a helpless infant at exactly the right time and in the right form.

questions.question: What conclusion should a thoughtful person draw from that example?
questions.answer: That such fitting and tender provision points to a Merciful Creator.

questions.question: What does it mean that the earth proclaims faith “according to the size” of its pages?
questions.answer: It means every part of the earth gives witness in a way suited to its own scale and content.

questions.question: Summarize the traveler’s final understanding from this section.
questions.answer: He sees the earth as a many-layered witness that declares Allah’s mercy, power, and oneness.

questions.question: What change of focus happens at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The traveler turns from the heavens to the earth to continue his search for signs.

questions.question: What does the image of a turning dervish add to the description of the globe?
questions.answer: It gives a sense of lively, graceful motion while still pointing to a meaningful pattern.

questions.question: Why is the earth compared to a vessel carrying supplies?
questions.answer: Because it supports and transports everything needed for the lives of many creatures.

questions.question: How does the example of babies and mothers make the argument more personal?
questions.answer: It brings the sign of mercy into everyday human experience where need and care are very clear.
